title: Melodic trombonist, plunger and the blues
summary: Jackson says he is mainly melodic but gets soulful with the plunger, credits Duke for the blues, and calls Hodges the greatest blues saxophonist.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: Well, you know, I've always been a melodic trombone player to a great extent with the exception of when I get that plunger in my hand. Then my mind goes filthy. It gets soulful then because I like blues, too, and

if you played with Duke Ellington any length of time, you will know to play the blues. Of course, I've always liked the blues anyway; regardless of being a melodic trombone player, I liked to listen to anybody that played the blues if they could play the blues. To me Johnny Hodges was the greatest blues saxophone player. Outside of being a melodic saxophone player, he could get filthy too.
